text: Our second use case is about biology.
Interactions arise naturally in biology.
Genes produce proteins.
Proteins regulate the functions of other proteins.
Cells transmit signals to other cells.
Dysfunctional genes lead to pathological conditions that present themselves as observable phenotypes.
Some of these interactions are observed and measured by experimentalists.
Another class of graph relations represent human knowledge.
For example, an edge may denote anatomical associations
such as the nucleus is inside a cell
or that the cerebral cortex is part of the brain.
Similarly, one can encode different classifications
of entities like both humans and dogs and mammals.
Researchers also find these relationships
from literature or by computational techniques
like bioinformatics algorithms.
There are many bioinformatics algorithms
that find statistical correlations
between genes and proteins.
Many biological networks are created
by creating edges between entities
because they are strongly correlated based on measurements,
like gene expression level.
Yet a third category of computer relationships
associates terms by minding scientific literature.
If two entities are co-mentioned in scientific articles very often,
then there is a likelihood that these two entities are related.
In this case, the edge between them does not depict a specific relationship
but the fact that they are associated.
All these interactions can be assembled into networks or graphs
where the nodes are biological entities
And edges represent different categories
of molecular interactions, associations
between diseases and genes.
